node.statement: Coarse-to-sharp C*-norm bootstrap and conclusion. Use the following elementary uniform lemma. If W:D->E is a star-preserving d-homomorphism from an exact C*-algebra to an epsilon-C*-algebra and c||z||<=||Wz||<=C||z|| with fixed 0<c<=C, then, for d+epsilon small, (1-K_b(d+epsilon))||z||<=||Wz||<=(1+K_b(d+epsilon))||z||, where K_b depends only on c,C. Indeed normalize ||z||=1, put z_0=z, z_{m+1}=z_m^dagger z_m, so ||z_m||=1, and a_m=||Wz_m|| lies in [c,C]. Multiplicative defect and the target C*-bounds give (1-epsilon)a_m^2-d<=a_{m+1}<=(1+epsilon)a_m^2+d. Hence |log a_{m+1}-2log a_m|<=K_0(d+epsilon). Iterating, dividing by 2^N, and letting N->infinity (the bounded term 2^{-N}log a_N vanishes) yields |log a_0|<=K_0(d+epsilon), which exponentiates to the claimed 1+/-K_b(d+epsilon) bounds after a universal threshold reduction. Apply this to every V_n using nodes 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 with d=K_alg*t and epsilon<=t. Thus all V_n satisfy the same K_inc*t homomorphism and two-sided norm clauses, and V_n=I_n tensor V by construction, proving node 1.2.
